one_line.text: British advertising executive, writer, and applied behavioural-science advocate known for using psychology to identify small contextual changes that alter consumer behaviour.

biography.text: Sutherland is President Emeritus of Ogilvy Consulting. He joined Ogilvy & Mather in 1988, moved from planning into copywriting, and spent more than twenty years as a copywriter and creative director before helping establish the firm's behavioural consulting work. He has served as President of the Institute of Practitioners in Advertising, spoken at TED, written The Spectator's Wiki Man column, and presented BBC Radio 4 series.

background.text: TED describes an early period as a classics teacher before Sutherland joined Ogilvy's planning department in 1988 and became a junior copywriter on Microsoft's account. Ogilvy records his later work as a copywriter, creative director, and founder of a practice seeking small, overlooked changes in consumer context. His career also includes early advocacy of digital media and extensive public communication through talks and columns.

expertise.text: His strongest evidence of expertise is long practical experience in advertising, branding, direct response, creative work, and applied behavioural consulting. He translates concepts from behavioural economics, evolutionary psychology, and perception into commercial and public-policy experiments. The cited biographies do not establish an academic research appointment or advanced qualification in psychology or economics.

perspective_and_limits.text: Sutherland writes as an advertising practitioner and persuasive public thinker. That gives him a large supply of real-world cases and sensitivity to framing, but it also favours memorable examples and hypothesis generation over systematic literature review, causal estimation, or formal theory. His authority is strongest on creative and behavioural problem-framing; technical scientific claims still need independent subject-matter checking.
